title: Constant section properties
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $R$ a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For an $R$-module $M$, let $\underline M$ be its constant sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf]. For every $U\in\mathcal C$: (1) the functor $M\mapsto\underline M(U)$ preserves short exact sequences of $R$-modules; (2) if $Q$ has a finite presentation $R^s\to R^t\to Q\to0$, the canonical map $\underline M(U)\otimes_R Q\to\underline{M\otimes_R Q}(U)$ is an isomorphism, natural in $M,Q,U$; (3) if $M$ is flat over $R$, meaning that tensoring with $M$ preserves injections, then $\underline M(U)$ is flat over $R$.

proof.text: By the definition of the constant sheaf, the constant presheaf sequence sheafifies to the displayed sequence of constant abelian sheaves. The module-sheafification interface identifies the underlying abelian sheaf with abelian sheafification, and the arbitrary-site sheafification exactness and sectionwise-limit statement gives exactness after evaluation at every U. For surjectivity, choose a set-theoretic section s:C→B; functoriality of the constant-sheaf construction gives a morphism of sheaves of sets underline C→underline B splitting the quotient, so its component at U supplies the required section. Thus M↦underline M(U) preserves short exact sequences.

Choose a finite presentation R^s → R^t → Q → 0. Right exactness of tensor product gives M^s → M^t → M tensor_R Q → 0. Applying the sectionwise exact constant-sheaf sequence from step 1 at U gives underline M(U)^s → underline M(U)^t → underline(M tensor_R Q)(U) → 0; evaluation commutes with these finite direct sums. The cokernel of the first map is, by the defining finite-presentation cokernel description of tensor product, underline M(U) tensor_R Q. This identifies the canonical map, and all constructions commute with maps in M, Q, and restriction in U.

Let I be a finitely generated ideal of R. The existing Noetherian finite-module presentation result makes I finitely presented. The finite-presentation tensor argument, using the cited tensor right-exactness statement and the arbitrary-site sectionwise exactness statement, identifies underline M(U) tensor_R I with underline(M tensor_R I)(U). Flatness of M makes M tensor_R I → M injective, so the constant-sheaf exactness result makes the induced map on sections injective. Since R is commutative, the symmetry of tensor identifies this map with the criterion map I tensor_R underline M(U) → R tensor_R underline M(U) under the canonical unit identification R tensor_R underline M(U) ≅ underline M(U). The existing finitely-generated-ideal criterion therefore implies that underline M(U) is flat.
